Topic 3.2: Reading readiness skills

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading readiness skills. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when (2HRS) a) Demonstrate left-right eye and drop from left to right in a digital clip. reading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. Demonstrate top-down activity and guided to turn pages from right to left. turn pages orientation skills when reading. •

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING READINESS SKILLS
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading readiness skills helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING READINESS SKILLS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Demonstrate top-down activity and guided to turn pages from right to left. turn pages orientation skills when reading. •

What this means
In this part you learn to Demonstrate top-down activity and guided to turn pages from right to left. turn pages orientation skills when reading. •. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Demonstrate top-down activity and guided to turn pages from right to left. turn pages orientation skills when reading. •.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading readiness skills”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Demonstrate top-down activity and guided to turn pages from right to left. turn pages orientation skills when reading. •. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading readiness skills is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading readiness skills”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Demonstrate top-down activity and guided to turn pages from right to left. turn pages orientation skills when reading. •)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading readiness skills to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Demonstrate top-down activity and guided to turn pages from right to left. turn pages orientation skills when reading. •.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading readiness skills from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading readiness skills: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Reading readiness skills?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when (2HRS) a) Demonstrate left-right eye and drop from left to right in a digital clip. reading?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading readiness skills means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Demonstrate top-down activity and guided to turn pages from right to left. turn pages orientation skills when reading. •.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
